Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(sandwich); library(lmtest)   # robust SEs

prime_age_laborforce_data <- d_HHP2020_24 %>% filter(!is.na(work_kind) &
                                                       Age >= 25 & Age <= 55)

# 1. Log income: coefficients become approx. % differences
prime_age_laborforce_data <- prime_age_laborforce_data %>%
  filter(income_midpoint > 0) %>%
  mutate(log_income = log(income_midpoint))

model_2 <- lm(log_income ~ Age + Gender + Education + Race,
              data = prime_age_laborforce_data)

# 2. Age is probably nonlinear (earnings rise, then flatten)
model_3 <- lm(log_income ~ Age + I(Age^2) + Gender + Education + Race,
              data = prime_age_laborforce_data)

# 3. Interactions: does the return to education differ by gender or race?
model_4 <- lm(log_income ~ Age + I(Age^2) + Gender * Education + Race,
              data = prime_age_laborforce_data)

# 4. Subsamples
females <- filter(prime_age_laborforce_data, Gender == "female")
college <- filter(prime_age_laborforce_data,
                  Education %in% c("college grad", "adv degree"))

model_f <- lm(log_income ~ Age + I(Age^2) + Education + Race, data = females)
model_c <- lm(log_income ~ Age + I(Age^2) + Gender + Race,    data = college)

# 5. Robust standard errors (and survey weights if the data has them)
coeftest(model_3, vcov = vcovHC(model_3, type = "HC1"))
# model_w <- lm(..., weights = pweight)   # check for a weight variable
```

```{r}
profiles <- expand.grid(Age = c(25, 35, 45, 55), Gender = "female", Race = "Black",
                        Education = c("some college", "adv degree"))
profiles$M1 <- predict(model_1, profiles)
profiles$M3 <- exp(predict(model_3, profiles))             # median-type prediction
smear <- mean(exp(residuals(model_3)))                       # Duan smearing factor
profiles$M3_mean <- profiles$M3 * smear                      # mean-type prediction
profiles
```

```{r}
chk <- data.frame(Age = c(30, 40, 50), Gender = "female", Race = "Black", Education = "adv degree")
chk$M1        <- predict(model_1, chk)
chk$M3_median <- exp(predict(model_3, chk))
chk$M3_mean   <- chk$M3_median * mean(exp(residuals(model_3)))
chk
```

```{r}
library(FNN)

dat <- prime_age_laborforce_data %>%
  select(income_midpoint, Age, Gender, Education, Race) %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  mutate(across(c(Gender, Education, Race), factor))   # keeps existing level order if already factors

X <- model.matrix(~ Age + Gender + Education + Race, data = dat)[, -1]   # dummies, drops intercept
y <- dat$income_midpoint

age_mean <- mean(X[, "Age"]); age_sd <- sd(X[, "Age"])
X[, "Age"] <- (X[, "Age"] - age_mean) / age_sd                          # standardize age
```

```{r}

set.seed(2000)
train <- sample(nrow(X), 0.8 * nrow(X))
test  <- sample(setdiff(seq_len(nrow(X)), train), 5000)   # 5,000 test rows keeps it fast

ks <- c(5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 200)
rmse <- sapply(ks, function(k) {
  pred <- knn.reg(train = X[train, ], test = X[test, ], y = y[train], k = k)$pred
  sqrt(mean((y[test] - pred)^2))
})
data.frame(k = ks, rmse = rmse)
best_k <- ks[which.min(rmse)]

plot(ks, rmse, type = "b", xlab = "k", ylab = "Test RMSE")
```

```{r}
make_X <- function(Age, Gender, Education, Race) {
  nd <- data.frame(Age = Age,
                   Gender = factor(Gender, levels = levels(dat$Gender)),
                   Education = factor(Education, levels = levels(dat$Education)),
                   Race = factor(Race, levels = levels(dat$Race)))
  m <- model.matrix(~ Age + Gender + Education + Race, data = nd,
                    contrasts.arg = lapply(dat[c("Gender", "Education", "Race")], contrasts, contrasts = FALSE) |> 
                      (\(x) NULL)())[, -1, drop = FALSE]
  m[, "Age"] <- (m[, "Age"] - age_mean) / age_sd
  m
}
```

```{r}
make_X <- function(newdata) {
  newdata$income_midpoint <- NA
  for (v in c("Gender", "Education", "Race"))
    newdata[[v]] <- factor(newdata[[v]], levels = levels(dat[[v]]))
  both <- rbind(newdata[, names(dat)], dat)
  m <- model.matrix(~ Age + Gender + Education + Race, data = both)[, -1]
  m[, "Age"] <- (m[, "Age"] - age_mean) / age_sd
  m[seq_len(nrow(newdata)), , drop = FALSE]
}

profiles_knn <- data.frame(Age = c(30, 40, 50), Gender = "female",
                           Race = "Black", Education = "adv degree")

profiles_knn$knn <- knn.reg(train = X, test = make_X(profiles_knn),
                            y = y, k = best_k)$pred
profiles_knn
```
